meta.rule: One visual language: every image on this site is an engraved, two-colour editorial illustration. No photographic imagery, because a photograph beside a buy button reads as a photograph of that product, and none of these images is a photograph of a product. Never depicts a brand mark, never implies a price or a feature the listing does not state.
meta.history: Before 2026-11-20 this register described the images as 'illustrative editorial photography', and the asset set did not match that description: eight of the seventeen files in use were photorealistic renders, including the images on product pages P-02 and P-04 and the seasonal feature. Those were replaced this session with engravings in the same style as the rest, and the rule was tightened to describe what the set actually is.
meta.why: The brief asks for a polished, image-led storefront. There is a real tension in that: Amazon's Program Policies bar misleading claims about a Product, and an AI-generated 'photo' of a product placed next to a buy button reads to most shoppers as a photo of that product. This page states the rule the site follows so a reviewer can challenge it.

rejected.idea: Use the listing's own product photography as the card image
rejected.why_not: Amazon's Program Content rules and the IP licence govern use of listing images and require them to come through permitted Program Content channels. Without PA API or Creators API access there is no permission basis for this build to copy them, so they are not used.

rejected.idea: Fetch each listing's live price on page load
rejected.why_not: Explicitly outside what the Program Policies permit without Amazon-served data or API access, and it would also be a third-party request from the reader's browser.

rejected.idea: Put a star rating next to each card
rejected.why_not: Same clause. Also unciteable: ratings change and this build cannot timestamp them from a permitted feed.
